title: Mass cytometry and random forests identify MCL-1 inhibitor plus dexamethasone synergy
summary: Mass cytometry probes for 26 cell-death, mitosis and signaling regulators profiled myeloma cells treated with dexamethasone or bortezomib. Random forest models ranked parameters separating survival from apoptosis, with phosphorylated CREB and MCL-1 defining surviving cells and predicting synergy between an MCL-1 inhibitor and dexamethasone. The synergy was confirmed in other cell lines, in vivo preclinical models and primary patient myeloma samples; the work is preclinical and has no clinical trial result.
ai_technology: Random forest models on single-cell mass cytometry data to predict a drug combination
organization: The University of Melbourne; Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research

evidence.tested: The predicted MCL-1 inhibitor and dexamethasone combination was tested in cell lines, preclinical in vivo models and primary patient samples.
evidence.unknown: Clinical efficacy and safety of the combination; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest models ranked survival determinants and predicted the synergistic combination.
